passage: Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine. Several recent studies have found that even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful {{1}}  on health. Still, the idea that exercising for just 10 minutes a week may be enough to increase your lifespan is novel. It's also somewhat ,  {{2}} since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of  {{3}} exercise each week. The study was based on data from more than 88,000 U.S. adults who  {{4}} in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008. Contrary to some research that has found an  {{5}} limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, the researchers found that there was {{6}}  no limit to the longevity( 长寿) benefits of exercise. Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower  {{7}} of death than the least active group. Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find {{8}}  . The researchers also were not able to  {{9}} for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time. Despite these ,  {{10}} the study's results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts.
